title: Probabilistic semantics from deterministic reachability
statement: Let a nondeterministic register program, oracle, input, guard, reached state $l'$, register valuation $v'$, and rational $p$ be given. Suppose the configuration $(l',v',	ext{no answer})$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $p$. Then, for every natural number $T$ and configuration $a$, if running the program with each choice resolved as false for $T$ steps takes $a$ to $(l',v',	ext{no answer})$, and the guard holds at every configuration along that run before time $T$, the initial configuration $a$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $p$.
hypotheses_covered: The reached configuration $(l',v',\text{no answer})$ has probabilistic semantics with probability $p$
The deterministic run with choices resolved as false reaches $(l',v',\text{no answer})$ after $T$ steps
The guard holds at every run configuration at times $t<T$
